evidence: Scope: manual source review of check 15, not a Docker build or full configured judge run. Read the actual frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx with openpyxl: Quality Checks!row 16 requires an agent image that is pinned, pre-installs every runtime dependency without runtime installation, and stages assets. Internal Quality Checks!row 16 repeats this wording and has no additional annotation. Deterministic Checks!rows 9, 10, 11 and 32 establish the related image/COPY/dependency interpretation, including unpinned apt being NOTE rather than failure. The frozen skill references/quality-checks.md:66-67 specifies express@5.1.0, better-sqlite3@12.4.1, matching NODE_PATH, COPY of notes/assets, a+rX, and an initialized empty /app. All task paths below are relative to .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/. environment/Dockerfile:1 uses 'FROM node:22-bookworm-slim', the identical base selection in the frozen template; this is version-tag selection under the supplied profile, not an immutable digest claim. The entire Dockerfile is byte-identical to rules/projects/webdev-task-template/environment/Dockerfile (both SHA256 0a75419e9598ded9317b26bbf0d2b12de0b9b11185fb4c9fed1ca7f3e52467d1). Dockerfile:3 sets 'ENV NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules'; :9-12 installs 'express@5.1.0' and 'better-sqlite3@12.4.1' globally during image build. Those are exactly the runtime dependencies in solution/app/package.json:13-16 and the only non-builtin imports in solution/app/server.js:2-5 (node:path, node:fs, express, better-sqlite3). tests/Dockerfile:9,20-21 provides the same path and package versions in the grading image. Dockerfile:14-16 copies both complete directories and applies 'chmod -R a+rX /instructions /assets'. I inspected all six actual instructions (behaviour, integration, overview, policy, security, ui) and the real seed_data.json; all seven source files exist, and their COPY directories are present. Dockerfile:17-23 creates /app, initializes git, and commits only .gitkeep; :25-26 selects /app and sleep infinity. No active COPY/ADD brings solution/ or tests/ into that image. integration.md:3,5,9,11 declares the same Node server/dependency/start contract, requires built frontend delivery, and says 'Starting the app mustn't install packages.' solution/app/package.json:7 starts 'node server.js'; its TypeScript/Vite entries at :17-19 are build-only. solution/solve.sh:26 only copies the supplied app tree after its database checks; server.js has no package installation path. public/index.html:1-2 references both existing built assets, and the compiled JS has no top-level external module import; source app/runtime imports resolve through shipped local files. Read-only assertions verified the dependency set, version strings, path, asset COPYs, permissions, workspace initialization, prohibited source COPY absence, and no start-time installation. An in-memory removal of better-sqlite3 or the assets COPY was detected by these assertions. Independently hashed all 50 task files and all 34 frozen rule files against manifest.json; zero mismatches. raw-evidence-index.json was read for scope: its supplied evidence is scripted golden work and explicitly lacks a full configured verifier. No fresh Docker build/image inspection was authorized or performed; this Pass is limited to the declared-world source contract, not a claim that current registry downloads or native package installation were executed successfully.
counterexample: Conforming alternative: a developer uses Vite/TypeScript only to compile the frontend and delivers ordinary built JS/CSS, then starts node /app/server.js with Express/better-sqlite3. Requiring Vite/TypeScript globally at runtime would falsely fail this allowed implementation; the actual package.json labels them devDependencies and the actual public/index.html points to delivered bundles. Broken alternative: keep an otherwise convincing Dockerfile but remove better-sqlite3@12.4.1, or omit COPY assets/ /assets/. The first makes server.js:5 unresolved in the declared runtime; the second loses the promised seed. I tried both removals in memory and the explicit dependency/COPY checks rejected them. Neither defect exists in the frozen candidate.
